question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: last 5 NVIDIA next-quarter guides vs just-reported actual, ratio 1.115-1.156 (median ~1.13). Q3 FY27 actual likely ~$111-115B given recent 3.6%/5.7% beats on guide and Polymarket Q3 DC pricing (~84% >$100B, 28% >$105B; thin, near-miss contract — evidence only). 1.13 x ~112.5 = ~$127B. Consensus Q4 ~$124-127B; NVDA guides have topped consensus by ~4%, but supply constraints (CFO: bottleneck through FY28) and China exclusion limit upside. Rubin ramp and 70% FY28 growth talk give upside tail. No market prices the Q4 guide itself.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (ended Jul 26 2026): revenue $96.2B (+18% q/q, +106% y/y), DC $89.0B; Q2 guide had been $91.0B ±2% (NVIDIA press release, Aug 26 2026).
- Q1 FY27 revenue $81.6B vs guide $78.0B; Q4 FY26 revenue $68.1B vs guide $65.0B (SEC 8-Ks).
- Guide history (guide midpoint / prior actual): Q3FY26 54.0/46.7; Q4FY26 65.0/57.0; Q1FY27 78.0/68.1; Q2FY27 91.0/81.6; Q3FY27 108.0/96.2 -> ratios 1.156, 1.140, 1.145, 1.115, 1.123.
- Recent beats vs own guide: Q1FY27 +4.6%, Q2FY27 +5.7%, Q4FY26 +4.8%.
- Q3 FY27 guide $108.0B ±2%, GM 74.0%, no China DC compute assumed (Q2 CFO commentary, Aug 26 2026). Pre-guide Q3 consensus was ~$103.8B.
- Vera Rubin production shipments began Aug 2026; ~20% of DC revenue in Q3 (tikr, Aug-Sep 2026). Mgmt preliminary FY28 growth ~70%; CFO: supply bottleneck through end of FY28.
- Supply commitments $279B (mostly memory); inventory $31.6B (Q2 CFO commentary).
- Aggregator consensus Q4 FY27 revenue ~$127B (search snippet, Oct 2026); FY27 total ~$412B implies Q3+Q4 ~$234B (AOL/Motley Fool Oct 18 2026).
- Risk side: 24/7 Wall St (Oct 19 2026) flags circular financing ($108.5B guarantees, ~$50B invested in AI labs), DSO rising to 60 days, margins bottoming 71-72%.
- Polymarket thin markets on Q3 DC revenue thresholds exist ($95B-$115B, volumes <$1k), not on Q4 guide.
- Status quo: NVIDIA issues a single-number ±2% guide in the Outlook section; resolves off the midpoint in Q3 FY27 press release (expected ~Nov 18-25 2026), not consensus or actuals.
- Event window: guide published in Q3 FY27 release (expected mid/late Nov 2026); as of Oct 19 2026 not yet published.
- Searched but not found: current sell-side Q4 guide expectations post-Q2, any market on Q4 guide itself.
calls.reference_class: NVIDIA next-quarter revenue guide midpoint / just-reported quarter actual, Q3 FY26-Q3 FY27 (5 quarters)

calls.reasoning: Over the last four quarters the guidance midpoint rose 17-20% from one guide to the next (54->65->78->91->108). Each guide was about 1.12-1.16x the prior quarter's actual, and actuals beat guidance by 4.6-5.7%. With Q3 actual around $113B, the Q4 guide comes out near 113 x 1.135 = ~$128B; the guide-to-guide step gives ~$126-130B. Lower: consensus for FY27 (~$412B) implies only ~$123B for Q4, memory costs are squeezing margins (expected 71-72% trough in Q4), China is excluded, and there is Vera Rubin execution risk. Higher: management targets ~70% FY28 growth, Rubin shipments began in August, and purchase commitments rose to $279B. Markets: no human market on the Q4 guide itself. Polymarket's low-volume Q3 Data Center contracts (>$100B at 0.84, >$105B at 0.28) imply total Q3 revenue of ~$109-113B, consistent with a typical beat; treated as evidence, not an anchor.

The criteria text says 'August 26, 2026', which appears to be a copy error; the Q3 release is expected mid/late November 2026 (sources conflict: Nov 17 call vs Nov 25).

Q3 actual expected ~$113-114B (12 straight beats above the top of the guide range; Q2 beat its guide by 5.7%), so ~113 x 1.12 gives ~126-128. Yahoo consensus for the Jan-2027 quarter averages $124.5B, and guides usually land 3-5% above consensus, pointing to ~128. Downside risks: supply limits, margins expected to bottom at 71-72%, and a possible pause in AI-lab financing. Upside: Rubin's higher revenue per gigawatt and a stronger hyperscaler Q4. No human market on the guidance itself; the Polymarket Q3 Data Center revenue contracts are thin and resolve on a different quantity.

calls.reference_class: NVIDIA quarterly revenue guidance midpoints FY2026-FY2027 relative to the prior guide and the prior quarter's actual

calls.reasoning: Base rate: NVIDIA's next-quarter guide midpoint has been 1.115-1.156x the just-reported actual over 5 quarters, and its actuals beat guidance by 4.6-5.7%. So Q3 actual is ~$113B and the Q4 guide ~113x1.12-1.135 = ~$126.5-128B. The guide-to-guide step (17-20%) gives $126-130B; consensus ~$124.5B plus the usual 2-4% guide-above-consensus gives ~$127-129B. Downside: supply constraints through FY28, China excluded, margins bottoming, falling ratio trend. Upside: Rubin ramp, a stronger hyperscaler Q4. No human market on the Q4 guide; Polymarket's thin Q3 DC threshold contracts only check Q3 ~$110-113B.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the facts: guide history 54/65/78/91/108, Q2 actual $96.2B, beat sizes 4.6-5.7%, ratio 1.115-1.156. The one factual dispute was the Q4 consensus level (~$127B snippet vs Yahoo $124.5B avg vs ~$123B implied by the FY27 $412B figure). Without web access it can't be settled; I weighted Yahoo's documented $124.5B (low 117, high 138) most. Judgment disputes: the Q3 actual estimate ($112.5-114B; I take ~$113B on beat history) and the multiplier (declining ratio trend vs 17-20% guide steps; I take ~1.125 with a slight upside skew from Rubin). Kept Run 2's dispersion basis (~$10B), which matches the reference-class spread; escape masses reflect a shock (supply/export/financing) on the low side and a big Rubin step-up on the high side.
